subject: MediSentry on-prem / air-gap recap & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Hall <lauren.hall@medisentry.com>, ops@medisentry.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: MediSentry on-prem / air-gap recap & proposed next steps

Hi Lauren / Medisentry ops team —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call + the items we said we'd follow up on. Please correct me if I mis-stated anything.

Pain points and drivers you shared:
- Regulated patient data (PHI) requires strict on-prem processing or a fully air-gapped deployment; no persistent egress of raw logs outside customer network.
- Need deterministic inference latency for triage model (~150 ms p95) and sustained throughput around 40–60 requests/sec during peak windows.
- Strong requirement to manage keys and encryption locally (customer-managed KMS/HSM).
- Procurement timeline: target pilot approval within 6–8 weeks; production procurement decision by end of Q3.

What we proposed on the call:
1) On‑prem, air-gapped option — package model artifacts and runtime for customer to host inside their data center / enclave. No outbound telemetry unless explicitly allowed (signed exception).
2) Private deployment in your cloud region with VPC isolation and customer-managed KMS — allows limited, auditable egress for updates/metrics to a pre-approved endpoint.
3) Dedicated hosted in Redwood Dedicated with strict routing and contractually bound data residency controls (we discussed this as lower preference for you).

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Lauren / ops: share the hardware spec (GPU type, NICs, storage layout) and procurement contact — goal: by 2027-04-15. (Attachment: medisentry_network_requirements.xlsx)
- Redwood (Marissa / Avery / me): prepare a detailed on‑prem checklist + a draft SOW for an air-gapped pilot that includes egress exceptions, telemetry plan, and acceptance criteria — deliver by 2027-04-16. (Attachments: redwood_onprem_checklist.pdf, draft_sow_template_v2.docx)
- Schedule a technical workshop with your infra and security teams to walk the checklist and confirm certificate/KMS flows — proposed slot: 2027-04-18 10:00–11:30 PT.

Risks / open questions we flagged:
- If absolutely no egress is allowed, our remote update and vulnerability scanning workflow will need an offline package process. That adds delivery overhead and changes pricing; will outline in the SOW.
- Licensing model for large models when served on-prem (we'll include license language options in the SOW).

Attachments referenced: medisentry_network_requirements.xlsx (you uploaded during the call), redwood_onprem_checklist.pdf (we'll fill), draft_sow_template_v2.docx (pricing placeholders).

If that all looks right, we'll lock the workshop for 4/18 and start the SOW draft. Happy to hop on a quick follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Hall <lauren.hall@medisentry.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T18:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MediSentry on-prem / air-gap recap & proposed next steps

Thanks Grace — this is a good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- We are operating under a contract that requires zero external egress of PHI. That means the "no egress" mode is our default. Any telemetry or remote management will require a formal exception and must be routed via our internal proxy / allowed endpoints only.
- Hardware: we'll be providing two servers with A40s (4x A40 per node) in an isolated VLAN. Networking is restricted; inbound only from our jump-hosts.
- KMS: we will use an on-prem HSM (Thales) for key material; Redwood will need to show how it integrates without sending keys off-site.
- Timeline: procurement prefers a short pilot (4–6 weeks) to validate performance before procurement signs the larger PO.

We will upload the hardware spec and a read-only network diagram to the shared Drive by end of day tomorrow. Also looping in our procurement lead (ops@medisentry.com) for SOW review.

Two asks for Redwood before the workshop:
1) In the SOW, please include an explicit clause about offline patch/update procedures for air-gapped deployments.
2) Provide a bullet list of the minimum telemetry we require to allow for safety/bug fixes (we're open to a very small, auditable set if behind a proxy).

Looking forward to the workshop on 4/18.

—Lauren
Lauren Hall
Head of Infrastructure, MediSentry
lauren.hall@medisentry.com
-- Attachment: medisentry_network_requirements.xlsx (XLSX, 60 KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Hall <lauren.hall@medisentry.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MediSentry on-prem / air-gap recap & proposed next steps

Lauren — thanks for the clarifications, very helpful. Short replies inline: 

- Air-gap default: understood. We'll prepare an "offline updates" playbook (how we package signed model/runtime updates and steps for applying them on your side). That will be part of the SOW/Appendix A.
- HSM integration: we'll outline an integration pattern that keeps key material in your HSM and uses a signing/verification flow for artifact integrity checks. No private keys leave your environment.
- Minimum telemetry list: we'll propose a narrow set (agent heartbeat, anonymized error codes, and signed operator-triggered logs). We'll make the default opt-out and document the exact endpoints (proxy-friendly).

Proposed workshop agenda for 2027-04-18 (10:00–11:30 PT):
1) Introductions & objectives (5 min)
2) Walk through network and hardware spec (15 min)
3) HSM/KMS integration pattern & key lifecycle (20 min)
4) Offline update playbook and SOW outline (20 min)
5) Next steps / procurement checkpoints (15 min)

Marissa and Avery will own the SOW and technical appendix. We'll aim to deliver the first draft by EOD 2027-04-16 so your procurement lead has time to review before the workshop.

Do you want us to include cost ranges for the three deployment options in the draft, or keep them out until after the pilot?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
